title: 1966 AHSME Problem 35
statement: Let \(O\) be an interior point of triangle \(ABC,\) and let \(s_1=OA+OB+OC.\) If \(s_2=AB+BC+CA,\) then:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
neither \((A)\) nor \((B)\) nor \((C)\) nor \((D)\) applies to
every triangle

solutions.text:
Adding the three strict triangle inequalities \[ \begin{gathered} AB\lt OA+OB,\\ BC\lt OB+OC,\\ CA\lt OC+OA \end{gathered} \] gives \(s_2\lt2s_1.\)

For the upper bound, extend \(AO\) to \(D\) on \(BC.\) Then \(AO+OD\lt AC+CD\) and \(OB\lt OD+DB,\) so cancellation gives \(OA+OB\lt AC+CB.\) Cycling and adding yields \(2s_1\lt2s_2.\) Therefore \(s_1\gt \frac{s_2}{2}\) and \(s_1\lt s_2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Extend \(AO\) to side \(BC\) to prove \(OA+OB\lt AC+CB,\) and cycle
